# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🫱 ✌ 🫲 🤟 🫳]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

I see a bomb display reading 0, a white light, and three wires in order: yellow, green, blue. I’m reporting the complete visual state so Mute can apply the manual and direct Blind to the correct wire. Blind’s wave does not convey an actionable instruction to me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The display reads 0. The light is white. Wires from left to right are yellow, green, blue. Apply the manual and tell Blind exactly which wire to cut or what action to take.")
speak(to="blind", text="I see display 0, white light, and wires left to right: yellow, green, blue. Wait for Mute's manual-based instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🫳 👈]

The bomb’s light has changed from white to purple; the display remains 0, and the wires remain yellow, green, blue from left to right. I cannot hear Mute’s spoken interpretation, and the gestures received from Mute do not identify an action without an established code. I’ll report the updated visual state and ask Mute to send Blind the manual-based instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Update: the light is now purple. Display remains 0; wires remain left to right yellow, green, blue. Please send Blind the exact manual-based action.")
speak(to="blind", text="Update: light is purple; display is 0; wires left to right are yellow, green, blue. Please follow Mute's exact manual-based instruction.")
wait()
```

WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🫱 👇]

The light has changed again, now to red. The display remains 0, and the wire colors and order remain yellow, green, blue. Mute’s gestures still have no established meaning for me, so I cannot safely infer the manual’s instruction; I’ll relay the updated state and ask Mute to communicate the exact action to Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Update: light is red. Display remains 0; wires left to right remain yellow, green, blue. Please send Blind the exact manual-based action immediately.")
speak(to="blind", text="Update: light is red; display is 0; wires left to right are yellow, green, blue. Follow Mute's manual-based instruction.")
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🫲 👉]

The display is still 0 and the wires are unchanged, but the light has returned to white. Mute’s latest gesture sequence is ✌ 🫲 👉; I cannot safely infer its meaning, so I’ll describe it to Blind and ask Mute to state the actual operation plainly.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I see display 0, white light, and wires yellow, green, blue from left to right. I also see your gestures ✌ 🫲 👉. Please state the exact operation and target for Blind in words.")
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0, white light, wires left to right yellow, green, blue. Mute's visible sequence is a two-finger V sign, a left-facing hand, then a right-pointing finger. Do not act unless Mute gives an explicit manual-based instruction.")
wait()
```

DISPLAY [0]

WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🫳 👈]

The current state is display 0, purple light, and wires yellow, green, blue from left to right. Mute’s gesture sequence is the same as in Turn 1: 🤟 🫳 👈. I should relay that sequence exactly to Blind, along with the visual state, without inventing a meaning for it.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I see display 0, purple light, and wires left to right yellow, green, blue. I received your gesture sequence 🤟 🫳 👈.")
speak(to="blind", text="Current bomb state: display 0; light purple; wires left to right yellow, green, blue. Mute's gesture sequence is 🤟 🫳 👈. Use the manual to determine the required action; do not act on my description alone.")
```

The bomb is unchanged except for the light: display 0, red light, and wires yellow, green, blue from left to right. Mute’s gestures match Turn 3, but I cannot determine their meaning. I’ll give both teammates the current state and have Mute provide Blind with the manual’s precise instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current state: display 0, red light, wires left to right yellow, green, blue. Your gestures are ☝ 🫱 👇. Please give Blind the exact manual-based action in words.")
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0, red light, wires left to right yellow, green, blue. Please rely on Mute for the exact manual-based action and do not act on my report alone.")
```

LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🫲 👉]

The repeated gesture patterns align with the light color, and their first symbols are clear numeric gestures: white uses ✌, purple uses 🤟, and red uses ☝. For the current white light, ✌ indicates wire 2. With wires ordered yellow, green, blue, that is the green wire. The remaining gestures in the sequence may be confirmation or additional manual data, so I will state the inferred target cautiously and ask Blind to confirm through Mute before acting.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current light is white, display 0, wires yellow green blue. Your white sequence is ✌ 🫲 👉; I interpret the first symbol ✌ as wire 2, the green wire. Please confirm the exact action for Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0, white light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute's white sequence is ✌ 🫲 👉. I tentatively interpret this as targeting wire 2, green; wait for Mute's explicit confirmation before cutting.")
wait()
```

WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👈]

The display remains 0 and the wires remain yellow, green, blue from left to right. The light is purple. Mute now signals only 👈, which most naturally indicates the leftmost wire, wire 1 (yellow). I’ll pass that as the tentative action to Blind, while asking Mute to confirm verbally.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The light is purple, display 0, and wires are yellow, green, blue from left to right. Your signal 👈 appears to indicate the leftmost yellow wire. Please confirm the exact action for Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0, purple light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute signaled 👈, which appears to indicate the leftmost yellow wire. Await Mute's confirmation before acting.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👇]

The recurring gesture patterns reveal that Mute uses the final gesture to identify the wire: white ends with 👉 (wire 2), purple with 👈 (wire 1), and red with 👇 (wire 3). The current red-light signal is 👇, so the required target is wire 3, the blue wire. I’ll tell Blind to cut the blue wire, while also confirming the interpretation with Mute.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current display 0, red light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. I interpret your signal 👇 as wire 3, the blue wire. Please confirm.")
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0, red light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute's signal 👇 indicates wire 3. Cut the blue wire.")
wait()
```
